name: Hold every question in one reusable store and assemble papers and quizzes from it
priorityReason: Exams, online exams and quizzes all draw on it. Without one store the same question is written four times.

goal.capability: to keep every question I have used in one place and pull from it when I build a paper
goal.outcome: a question written once is available for ever, and nobody rewrites what the school already has

secondaryActors.involvement: Writes questions and assembles papers for any class or subject.

additional.description: A question is used in an exam paper or a quiz, which stores it in the bank automatically.

preconditions.condition: Classes and their subjects exist, since every question is stored against both.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is a Teacher or a Coordinator.

postConditions: Every question is stored with its class, its subject and its answer key, and stays available for reuse.
Any question used in an exam paper or a quiz was added to the bank automatically, whether or not anybody remembered to add it.
A paper or a quiz has been assembled from questions pulled out of the bank, or written new and added as they were used.
A teacher searching their own subject found what the school already holds rather than writing it again.
The paper was reviewed and finalised before being used for a printed exam, an online exam or a quiz.
There is one store. An online exam and a quiz drew on the same bank, and no separate multiple-choice store exists.
Nothing was deleted. A question no longer wanted is retired and stays attached to the papers that used it.

dataFields.name: Class
dataFields.validation: The class the question is for. Every question carries one (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Subject
dataFields.validation: The subject the question belongs to (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Question type
dataFields.validation: What kind of question it is.

dataFields.name: Question text
dataFields.example: State Newton's second law and give its mathematical form.

dataFields.name: Options
dataFields.validation: The choices offered, where the type is multiple choice.
dataFields.requiredWhen: The type is Multiple choice or True or false

dataFields.name: Answer key
dataFields.validation: The correct answer, or the marking points for a written question. Every question carries one (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Marks
dataFields.validation: What the question is worth. Greater than zero.

dataFields.name: Topic
dataFields.validation: Optional. Makes the bank searchable by what the question is about (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Times used
dataFields.validation: How often the question has appeared in a paper or a quiz.

dataFields.name: Last used
dataFields.validation: Which paper or quiz used it most recently, so a teacher can avoid repeating it.

dataFields.name: Retire reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required when a question is retired (BR-8).
dataFields.example: The syllabus changed and this topic is no longer taught.

businessRules.rule: Every question is stored with a class, a subject and an answer key. A question without those three cannot be found again or marked.
A topic and a difficulty may be recorded. They are optional, because a teacher entering a question during a busy week should not be blocked by taxonomy.
Any question used in an exam paper or in a quiz is stored in the bank automatically and stays available for reuse. Nobody has to remember to add it, which is why the bank actually fills.
A paper or a quiz is built by searching the bank by class and subject and pulling in the questions wanted.
A teacher works within their own subjects; the Coordinator works across any class or subject in their remit.
Either may write a question that is not already in the bank, and it is added to the bank as it is used. Writing a question and banking it are the same act.
This is the only question store in the module. An online exam and a quiz draw on this same bank, and there is no separate multiple-choice store.
A question is retired rather than deleted, with a reason, and stays attached to the papers that used it. Deleting it would leave a past paper unreadable.
The paper is reviewed and finalised before it is used, whether for a printed exam, an online exam or a quiz.
A finalised paper's questions are fixed. Changing a question afterwards produces a new version of the paper rather than altering one already sat.
The bank shows how often a question has been used and where it was last used, so a teacher can avoid repeating the same question in consecutive terms.
A question bank is never visible to a student or a guardian. A readable bank is a leaked paper.

transitions.condition: Retired with a reason. It stays attached to the papers that used it (BR-8).
Used for a printed exam, an online exam or a quiz (BR-10).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Examination → Question bank → Write question
basicFlow.userAction: Writes a question with its class, subject, answer key and marks, and optionally a topic and a difficulty.
basicFlow.function: createQuestion(classId, subjectId, type, text, options, answerKey, marks, topic, difficulty)
basicFlow.systemResponse: Stores it in the bank, requiring the class, the subject and the answer key.

basicFlow.navigation: Question bank → Build paper → Search the bank
basicFlow.userAction: Searches the bank by class and subject for what the school already holds.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns the matching questions with how often each has been used and where it was last used.

basicFlow.navigation: Build paper → Pull in a question
basicFlow.userAction: Pulls in the questions wanted and sets their order and marks.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Builds the paper from the bank.

basicFlow.navigation: Build paper → Write a new question
basicFlow.userAction: Writes a question not already in the bank.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Adds it to the bank as it is used, so writing and banking are one act.
Fixes the questions, after which a change produces a new version rather than altering one already sat.
Makes the paper available for a printed exam, an online exam or a quiz, from the one bank.

basicFlow.userAction: Retires a question no longer wanted, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Removes it from search while leaving it attached to the papers that used it.

alternateFlows.condition: The question needed is not in the bank
alternateFlows.navigation: Build paper → Write a new question
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is written and added to the bank as it is used, so the bank fills from actual use rather than from a separate cataloguing exercise (BR-3, BR-6).
alternateFlows.function: createQuestion(classId, subjectId, type, text, options, answerKey, marks, topic, difficulty)

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher wants to avoid repeating last term's questions
alternateFlows.behaviour: The bank shows how often each question has been used and where it was last used (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The paper was authored by a teacher
alternateFlows.behaviour: The Coordinator reviews it before finalising, so no paper reaches a hall unchecked (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The paper is for a quiz rather than an exam
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same bank and the same assembly serve a quiz. There is no separate multiple-choice store (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: A question is wrong or the syllabus has changed
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is retired with a reason and stays attached to the papers that used it, so a past paper is still readable (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A finalised paper needs a change
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new version of the paper is produced. A paper already sat is never altered (BR-10).

Running an online exam from the paper

departures.requirement: There is exactly one question store in the module. No screen, import or feature creates a second bank for any question type.
A question used anywhere is banked without a separate act, because a bank that depends on somebody remembering stays empty.
The bank is not reachable by a student or a guardian by any route, including a shared link or an export.
A search across 20,000 questions returns within 2 seconds, since it is used while building a paper.
Questions and papers are retained 7 years, so a past paper stays readable.

openQuestions.question: Should a teacher be able to see questions written by another teacher in the same subject?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes as modelled, since the bank is the school's. Confirm teachers are content with that.

openQuestions.question: Should the bank be shared across branches, or held per branch?
openQuestions.assumption: Per branch as modelled. A shared bank would be more useful and is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Is there any check that a paper does not repeat a question used in the previous term?
openQuestions.assumption: The usage figures are shown but nothing enforces it.

openQuestions.question: Who may retire a question written by somebody else?
Should papers themselves be access-controlled more tightly than the bank before an exam is sat?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a paper is more sensitive than a question.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
